parties:
Ful Meher Bibi being dead her heirs Sabura Khatun and others ------ Appellants
Vs.
Abdul Wahab and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Short facts are that the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 285 of 1980 for partition in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka, impleading Ful Meher  Bibi and thirteen others as the defendants. The suit was subsequently renumbered as Partition Suit No. 113 of 1991 on transfer. The suit land originally belonged to Sheikh Nazimuddin and Abdus Salam, sons of late Raizuddin in equal shares. Sheikh Nazimuddin died leaving behind one son, Abdur Rahman and one daughter, Amirjan. Plaintiffs are the heirs and successors of Abdus Salam who inherited to the extent of the other half of the suit land. The suit was ultimately decreed in preliminary and final form on 25.08.1992 and 05.07.1993 respectively, though the appellants claim that no summons of the original suit was served upon Ful Meher Bibi (defendant No.8). The case of the appellants is that Ful Meher Bibi was married more than forty years back and since then she had been residing at her husband's house. But the plaintiff respondents fraudulently obtained the ex-parte decree in question showing service of summons upon her by hanging at her paternal house instead of serving it at her husband's house where she was residing in order to deprive her from contesting the suit. The appellants further claim that the plaintiffs were fully aware of her correct address of Ful Meher Bibi as they are her co-sharers. The appellants came to know about the ex-parte decree when the process server went to the suit land for execution of the ex-parte decree passed in the above mentioned partition suit. The appellants then filed Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 1994 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the preliminary and final decrees in question and for restoration of the original suit to its original file and number. 

 3. The plaintiff respondents contested the miscellaneous case by filing written objection and denied the material allegations made in the miscellaneous petition. 

 4. The learned Subordinate Judge (now joint District Judge), Dhaka, allowed the miscellaneous case on the ground that summons of the original suit was not duly served upon Ful Meher Bibi and restored the suit to its original file and number. The respondent then filed Civil Revision No.2951 of 1998 before the High Court Division and the Rule issue was made absolute. The High Court Division while making the Rule absolute observed that the application under order 9 rule 13 was barred by limitation and no application for condonation of delay was filed. It was further observed that the preliminary decree of the original suit was passed on 25.08.1992 and the final decree was passed on 05.07.1993 but the application under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed on 09.03.1994. The High Court Division further noticed that one Md. Ramjan Ali had sworn affidavit as the nephew (sister's son) of Ful Meher Bibi but he did not turn up to depose in support of the application rather one Raham Ali claiming to be a nephew (brother's son) of Ful Meher Bibi deposed in the case under order 9 rule 13 of Code of Civil Procedure. It was further observed that after the death of Ful Meher Bibi, as claimed by Raham Ali, none of her children came before the court to support the application nor authorized Raham Ali to depose on their behalf. The High Court Division further observed that service by hanging is not uncommon in the country side. 

 5. Leave was granted to consider the submission that order V rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides, inter alia, that the serving officer of the summons shall affix a copy of the summons on the outer door or some other conspicuous part of the home in which the defendant ordinarily resides and in the present case copy of the summons not having been affixed on any part of the ordinary residence of the defendant No. 8 which is her husband's address and allegedly having affixed at her father's address which she left 40-45 years ago the alleged service by hanging at the father's address, is not a service as required by order V rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the next submission that the trial court found that the summons was not duly served upon defendant No.8, Ful Meher Bibi for the reasons stated in the order dated 07.06.1998 and this Court in the case of Government of Bangladesh represented by the Ministry of Works, Bangladesh Secretariat, Dhaka Vs. Chand Mia and others reported in 44 DLR (AD) 98 having held in paragraph 11 of the report, "By no stretch of imagination this point could have been of any concern to the High Court Division. The lower Appellate Court had given a finding that there was no service of summons upon the appellant in that suit. It was no function of the High Court Division to sit in appeal over that finding of the lower Appellate Court in the revisional jurisdiction. The High Court Division was only concerned with the question as to whether the lower court in giving that finding committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice," and the last submission that the High Court Division committed an error of law in holding that the application under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is barred by limitation in that in the facts of this case limitation is to be counted from the date of knowledge of defendant No. 8 under Article 164 of the Limitation Act as the summons was not duly served upon her. 

 13. In the instant case, undisputedly summons of the original suit upon defendant No.8, Ful Meher Bibi (since deceased) was not served by hanging on her dwelling but where she ordinarily resided nor summons was sent to that address rather the same was issued and alleged to have been served by hanging on the outer door of dwelling but of her paternal house where she did not reside for the last 40-45 years. The case of the appellant-petitioners in the case under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was that defendant No. 8 for the first time came to know of the ex parte decree on 09.02.1994 when the process server of the Court went to the locality to deliver possession of land in execution of the decree in question and thereafter she filed the case and from the date of her knowledge she was within time. 

 14. Mr. Bhuiyan submitted that since the case under Order 9 Rule 13 C.P.C. was tiled within 30 days from date of knowledge of the ex parte decree, the question of filing an application under "section 5 of the Limitation Act did not arise and the High Court Division was wrong in holding that since no application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay was filed, the trial court was not justified in allowing the case and setting aside the ex parte decree. 

 15. From our above discussions, we are of the view that the findings of the trial court are based on the materials on record that there was no service of summons upon Ful Meher Bibi, defendant No. 8 of the original suit. Therefore, it was no function of the High Court Division to sit in appeal over that finding of the trial court in revisional jurisdiction. We also find that the application order 9 rules 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not barred by limitation in the facts of this case as limitation is to be counted from the date of knowledge of defendant No. 8 under Article 164 of the Limitation Act as the summons was not duly served upon her.
